title: Load status groups the CPU consumers by kind and clone with a cause and a remedy each
goal: kbmon.py --status load reads one ps -A -o pid=,pcpu=,args= listing in the host panel and sorts each process by fixed patterns of its command line into the kinds kbmon, fseventsd, kb-tools, claude, tests and other, with clone this or other for the kb's own scripts; it prints the groups in CPU order with their CPU percent, process count, a cause and a remedy each, beside the load and cores; --json gives groups of kind, clone, cpu, procs, cause and remedy; no command line, argument or path of a process is printed or kept in the snapshot

gates.question: The sessions panel never reads a process's command line. May load status read it to sort a process into a kind (kbmon, kb tools, tests)?
options: read it in memory only, to match fixed patterns; print and keep only kind, clone, CPU and count
read only the command name, so every Python tool is one kind
gates.recommendation: read it in memory only, to match fixed patterns; print and keep only kind, clone, CPU and count
gates.answer: read it in memory only, to match fixed patterns; print and keep only kind, clone, CPU and count

notes: Plan 2026-10-19: premise: --status load exits 2 and the host panel has no process data. %CPU differs by platform (Linux procps: CPU time over the process's life; macOS: a decaying recent average; the goal research story confirms it), so the answer says which it shows. Windows has no ps: the groups are unsupported there. The remedies are fixed text, e.g. kbmon: a longer --interval or fewer live views; fseventsd: file churn in the clone and its worktrees, so fewer parallel workers and pruned worktrees; kb-tools: a long pack or index build, see stalled; claude: fewer parallel sessions; tests: one whole-suite run at a time (the host lock).
